components.note: 一 (line) — dictionary reads 不 as a bird flying up toward the sky 一. The meaning 'not' is a borrowing, so the shape does not explain it today.
杯 (bēi) — a character that uses 不 as a loose sound clue (木 + 不). The sound is a hint only: 不 bù vs bēi.
口 (mouth) — speech or assent: to say "OK". 可 is also a famous sound part: 河 hé, 歌 gē, 哥 gē, 何 hé all take their sound from it.
田 here replaces 囟 (skull) in the older form: head over heart
心 (heart) — thinking and feeling, as in 想, 意, 感: 思 is to think over, with head and heart.
讠 (speech, simplified 言) — talking and language: 说 say, 请 ask, 话 speech; 议 is to discuss.
义 (yì) sounds exactly like 议; same part in 仪 yí and 蚁 yǐ.

example.hanzi: 这个魔术表演真是不可思议。
example.pinyin: Zhège móshù biǎoyǎn zhēnshi bùkěsīyì.
example.english: This magic performance is truly incredible.
example.fact: 不可思议 is often traced to Buddhist sutra translation, where it rendered a Sanskrit term for a truth beyond ordinary conception — thought (思) and discourse (议) alike fall short of grasping it. The everyday modern sense, "unbelievable, incredible," is a secularized descendant of that religious original.

examples.hanzi: 这个结果真是不可思议!
examples.pinyin: Zhège jiéguǒ zhēnshi bùkěsīyì!
examples.english: This result is simply unbelievable!

examples.hanzi: 他一个人跑完全程,简直不可思议。
examples.pinyin: Tā yí ge rén pǎowán quánchéng, jiǎnzhí bùkěsīyì.
examples.english: He ran the whole course alone, which is almost incredible.

components.note: 纟 (silk thread, simplified 糸) — threads and ties, as in 红, 给, 经; 结 is a knot.
吉 (jí) is a close sound clue for jié; 吉 also sounds out 洁 jié.

example.hanzi: 他们去年结婚了。
example.pinyin: Tāmen qùnián jiéhūn le.
example.english: They got married last year.
example.fact: 结 is read jié (to tie, to conclude: 结婚, 结束) and jiē (to bear fruit). 结果 is jiéguǒ meaning "result" but jiēguǒ meaning "bear fruit", a famous minimal pair. Its noun sense is a knot: 打结.

examples.hanzi: 他们结了婚，住在一起。
examples.pinyin: Tāmen jié le hūn, zhù zài yìqǐ.
examples.english: They got married and live together.

examples.hanzi: 她把头发结成了辫子。
examples.pinyin: Tā bǎ tóufa jié chéng le biànzi.
examples.english: She tied her hair into a braid.

components.note: 父 (father) — 父 marks older male relatives, as in 爸 dad; 爷 is grandfather.
耶 (yé) — the old form 爺 had 耶 giving the sound yé — the simplified 爷 keeps just a trace of it.
父 (father) — 父 marks older male relatives, as in 爸 dad; 爷 is grandfather.
耶 (yé) — the old form 爺 had 耶 giving the sound yé — the simplified 爷 keeps just a trace of it.

example.hanzi: 爷爷每天早上都去公园散步。
example.pinyin: Yéye měitiān zǎoshang dōu qù gōngyuán sànbù.
example.english: Grandpa goes for a walk in the park every morning.
example.fact: Chinese kinship terms distinguish sides of the family where English doesn't: 爷爷 is specifically the father's father, while the mother's father is 外公 — the "outer" 外 marking the maternal side as literally "outside" the family line.

examples.hanzi: 爷爷给我讲了很多过去的故事。
examples.pinyin: Yéye gěi wǒ jiǎng le hěn duō guòqù de gùshi.
examples.english: Grandpa told me many stories from the past.

examples.hanzi: 我周末要去看爷爷。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ zhōumò yào qù kàn yéye.
examples.english: I'm going to visit my grandpa this weekend.

components.note: 会 (meet, can) — simplified from 會, a lid on a container: bringing things together; hence meeting, then "can" (huì).
儿 (child, legs) — shows a person's legs; in 兒 the top was a child's soft skull. As an ending (这儿) it adds the er sound; 儿 also in 先, 兄, 光.

example.hanzi: 你等我一会儿,我马上就来。
example.pinyin: Nǐ děng wǒ yíhuìr, wǒ mǎshàng jiù lái.
example.english: Wait for me a moment, I'll come right away.
example.fact: 会儿 almost never stands alone — it's the second half of set phrases like 一会儿 ("in a moment") and 这会儿 ("right now"), and its r-suffix (儿化) marks it as northern, colloquial Mandarin; more formal writing tends to avoid it.

examples.hanzi: 我想休息一会儿。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng xiūxi yíhuìr.
examples.english: I want to rest for a little while.

examples.hanzi: 请再等一会儿,马上就好。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng zài děng yíhuìr, mǎshàng jiù hǎo.
examples.english: Please wait a bit longer, it'll be ready soon.

components.note: 止 (foot) — a foot heading straight for a target line: upright, correct. 正 gives sound to 证 zhèng, 整 zhěng and 政 zhèng.
弋 (yì) is a loose sound clue for shì; 弋 also in 试 shì and 拭 shì.
工 (work, craft) — a craftsman's pattern, a standard.

example.hanzi: 会议将在下周正式开始。
example.pinyin: Huìyì jiāng zài xià zhōu zhèngshì kāishǐ.
example.english: The meeting will officially begin next week.
example.fact: 正式 pairs a "correct, proper" root (正) with a "style, pattern" root (式) — together, "conforming to the proper pattern." Its antonym 非正式 ("informal") simply negates the same compound with 非 rather than swapping in an unrelated word, a common pattern in Chinese antonym formation.

examples.hanzi: 这家餐厅下个月正式营业。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā cāntīng xià ge yuè zhèngshì yíngyè.
examples.english: This restaurant officially opens next month.

examples.hanzi: 面试时要穿正式的衣服。
examples.pinyin: Miànshì shí yào chuān zhèngshì de yīfu.
examples.english: You should wear formal clothes to an interview.

components.note: 厂 (shelter) — 厂 stands for a building or shelter, as here — 厨 is the room where food is cooked, in 厨房 kitchen and 厨师 chef.
户 (door) — doors and houses, as in 所 and 扇: a room with a door.
方 (fāng) is a close sound clue for fáng; 方 also sounds out 放 fàng and 访 fǎng.

example.hanzi: 妈妈在厨房里做饭。
example.pinyin: Māma zài chúfáng lǐ zuòfàn.
example.english: Mom is cooking in the kitchen.
example.fact: 房 is Mandarin's general word for a room within a building (卧房 "bedroom," 书房 "study"), and 厨 narrows it specifically to cooking — the same transparent "room for X" logic runs through most Chinese words for rooms.

examples.hanzi: 厨房里有一股好闻的香味。
examples.pinyin: Chúfáng lǐ yǒu yì gǔ hǎowén de xiāngwèi.
examples.english: There is a nice smell in the kitchen.

examples.hanzi: 我们新家的厨房很干净。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen xīn jiā de chúfáng hěn gānjìng.
examples.english: The kitchen in our new home is very clean.

components.note: 牛 (ox) — cattle and animals, as in 物 thing, 牧 herd, 牺 sacrifice: 特 first meant a bull, then special.
寺 (sì) is only a loose sound clue for tè; 寺 also in 诗 shī and 持 chí.
歹 (death, bad) — 歹 is the "bad or death" radical, in 死, 残; 殊 first meant to cut off, then different, special.
朱 (zhū) — near sound — 殊 is shū; 朱 also sounds out 株 zhū and 珠 zhū.

example.hanzi: 这是一个特殊的情况,我们需要特别处理。
example.pinyin: Zhè shì yí gè tèshū de qíngkuàng, wǒmen xūyào tèbié chǔlǐ.
example.english: This is a special situation; we need to handle it specially.
example.fact: 特 traces back to a male ox singled out for ritual sacrifice, set apart from the rest of the herd — an image of being "picked out" that survives abstractly in both 特殊 ("out of the ordinary") and 特别 ("especially"), built on the same root.

examples.hanzi: 今天是个特殊的日子。
examples.pinyin: Jīntiān shì ge tèshū de rìzi.
examples.english: Today is a special day.

examples.hanzi: 他的身体有些特殊,不能吃辣的。
examples.pinyin: Tā de shēntǐ yǒuxiē tèshū, bù néng chī là de.
examples.english: His body is a bit unusual and he can't eat spicy food.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — marks actions done by hand, as in 打, 拉, 提; 扯 is to tear or pull.
止 (zhǐ) is a loose hint for chě.

example.hanzi: 别扯我的衣服。
example.pinyin: Bié chě wǒ de yīfu.
example.english: Don't pull on my clothes.
example.fact: 扯 starts as a physical pull, then becomes colloquial for rambling: 瞎扯 (talk nonsense), 闲扯 (chat idly), 扯淡 (rubbish, crude). 扯后腿 means to hold someone back.

examples.hanzi: 他一直扯着我的手不放。
examples.pinyin: Tā yìzhí chě zhe wǒ de shǒu bú fàng.
examples.english: He kept pulling my hand and wouldn't let go.

examples.hanzi: 别扯远了，我们说正事。
examples.pinyin: Bié chě yuǎn le, wǒmen shuō zhèngshì.
examples.english: Don't go off topic; let's talk about the real matter.

components.note: 专 (zhuān) also gives its sound to 转 zhuǎn, 传 chuán, 砖 zhuān and 团 tuán (traditional 專).
Memory aid: 业 looks like a row of upright posts on a base, like a shop sign or an old tool stand; 'business/trade' is the extended meaning. Origin is unclear, so no firm etymology.

example.hanzi: 你在大学学的是什么专业?
example.pinyin: Nǐ zài dàxué xué de shì shénme zhuānyè?
example.english: What was your major in university?
example.fact: 专业 does double duty as both a noun ("major, specialized field") and an adjective ("professional, expert") — 他很专业 ("He's very professional") uses the same two characters as 我的专业 ("my major"), with word class inferred purely from position in the sentence.

examples.hanzi: 我哥哥学的是计算机专业。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ gēge xué de shì jìsuànjī zhuānyè.
examples.english: My older brother studies computer science.

examples.hanzi: 她对这个专业很感兴趣。
examples.pinyin: Tā duì zhège zhuānyè hěn gǎn xìngqù.
examples.english: She is very interested in this major.

components.note: 耂 (old) — 老 pictures an old person with long hair leaning on a staff; the short form 耂 is also in 考 test and 孝 filial.
宀 (roof) — houses and shelter, as in 家, 字, 室: a house stocked with goods, so solid and real.

example.hanzi: 他是一个很老实的人,从不说谎。
example.pinyin: Tā shì yí gè hěn lǎoshi de rén, cóngbù shuōhuǎng.
example.english: He's a very honest person who never lies.
example.fact: 老实 can flip from a compliment to a mild criticism depending on context — praising someone's honesty in one sentence, or gently mocking their naivety in the next (老实人 often implies someone too trusting for their own good) — a duality English "honest" doesn't carry.

examples.hanzi: 这个孩子很老实,不会骗人。
examples.pinyin: Zhège háizi hěn lǎoshi, bú huì piàn rén.
examples.english: This child is honest and won't lie.

examples.hanzi: 你老实告诉我,到底怎么回事?
examples.pinyin: Nǐ lǎoshi gàosu wǒ, dàodǐ zěnme huí shì?
examples.english: Tell me honestly, what really happened?

components.note: 日 (sun) — time and day, as in 早 early, 时 time, 明 bright; 晚 is when the sun is late.
免 (miǎn) is a close sound clue for wǎn; it also sounds out 勉 miǎn and 挽 wǎn.
饣 (food, simplified 食) — meals and eating: 饿 hungry, 饱 full, 饺 dumpling; 饭 is cooked rice or a meal.
反 (fǎn) is a near sound match for fàn; also in 板 bǎn.

example.hanzi: 我们一家人一起吃晚饭。
example.pinyin: Wǒmen yì jiā rén yìqǐ chī wǎnfàn.
example.english: Our whole family eats dinner together.
example.fact: 饭 literally means "cooked rice" before it means "meal" in general — 晚饭 ("evening rice"), 早饭 ("morning rice"), and 午饭 ("noon rice") all build on that same core word, a linguistic fossil of rice's central place in a traditional Chinese meal.

examples.hanzi: 今天的晚饭你想吃什么?
examples.pinyin: Jīntiān de wǎnfàn nǐ xiǎng chī shénme?
examples.english: What do you want for dinner today?

examples.hanzi: 吃完晚饭,我们一起去散步。
examples.pinyin: Chīwán wǎnfàn, wǒmen yìqǐ qù sànbù.
examples.english: After dinner, let's go for a walk together.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — breath and speech: 呼, 吃, 喝; 吸 is to breathe in.
及 (jí) is a loose sound hint for xī; same part in 级 jí and 极 jí.
弓 (bow) — the vertical stroke 丨 is the string being drawn back on a bow — 引 is to pull, then to attract and to cite.

example.hanzi: 这家博物馆吸引了很多游客。
example.pinyin: Zhè jiā bówùguǎn xīyǐn le hěn duō yóukè.
example.english: This museum attracts many tourists.
example.fact: 吸 (built around 口, "mouth") originally described breathing in air, and 引 (a bow 弓 with its string 丨 drawn back) meant "to pull" — 吸引 fuses "inhaling" and "pulling toward" into one vivid image of drawing something in.

examples.hanzi: 这首歌的旋律深深地吸引了我。
examples.pinyin: Zhè shǒu gē de xuánlǜ shēnshēn de xīyǐn le wǒ.
examples.english: The melody of this song really drew me in.

examples.hanzi: 他的笑容很吸引人。
examples.pinyin: Tā de xiàoróng hěn xīyǐn rén.
examples.english: His smile is very attractive.

components.note: 年 (year) — first drawn as a person carrying harvested grain: one harvest per year. Seen in 今年, 去年, 年轻.
亻 (person radical, 单人旁) — people and roles: 你, 他, 位; 代 is one person replacing another, then a generation.
弋 (yì) is only a loose hint; 代 itself sounds out 袋 dài and 贷 dài.

example.hanzi: 这首歌是八十年代的经典。
example.pinyin: Zhè shǒu gē shì bāshí niándài de jīngdiǎn.
example.english: This song is a classic from the eighties.
example.fact: 年代 has a distinctive use for naming a decade of a century — 八十年代 means "the eighties (1980s)," not "eighty years" — a construction that trips up learners used to English's simpler "the 80s."

examples.hanzi: 我爸爸是九十年代出生的。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ bàba shì jiǔshí niándài chūshēng de.
examples.english: My dad was born in the nineties.

examples.hanzi: 那个年代的人生活很简单。
examples.pinyin: Nà ge niándài de rén shēnghuó hěn jiǎndān.
examples.english: People in that era lived simple lives.

components.note: 士 (scholar, soldier) — usually read as an axe or weapon, so a warrior or gentleman (士兵, 博士). Memory aid: 士 has the longer bar on top, 土 (earth) on the bottom.
兵 (soldier) — old forms show two hands (the 八 at the bottom) holding an axe (the top, now written 丘), so weapons in hand means soldier.

example.hanzi: 这些士兵已经在边境驻守了三年。
example.pinyin: Zhèxiē shìbīng yǐjīng zài biānjìng zhùshǒu le sān nián.
example.english: These soldiers have been stationed at the border for three years.
example.fact: 兵 pictures hands gripping a weapon, and its root sense spans both "weapon" and the person who wields one — a double sense still visible in 兵器 ("weaponry") next to 士兵 ("soldier"), where the same character can point either to the gear or to the person carrying it.

examples.hanzi: 一个士兵正站在门口守卫。
examples.pinyin: Yí ge shìbīng zhèng zhàn zài ménkǒu shǒuwèi.
examples.english: A soldier is standing guard at the door.

examples.hanzi: 他从小就梦想当一名士兵。
examples.pinyin: Tā cóngxiǎo jiù mèngxiǎng dāng yì míng shìbīng.
examples.english: He has dreamed of becoming a soldier since he was little.

components.note: 艹 (grass, plants) — 艹 marks plants; 蓝 is the indigo plant from which blue dye was made.
监 (jiān) — loose hint — 蓝 is lán; 监 also sounds out 篮 lán and 滥 làn.

example.hanzi: 天空是蓝色的。
example.pinyin: Tiānkōng shì lánsè de.
example.english: The sky is blue.
example.fact: 蓝 first named the indigo plant. The classic saying 青出于蓝而胜于蓝 means the dye outshines the plant, so a student can surpass the teacher. 蓝牙 is Bluetooth and 蓝领 is blue-collar.

examples.hanzi: 我很喜欢蓝色的衣服。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ hěn xǐhuan lánsè de yīfu.
examples.english: I really like blue clothes.

examples.hanzi: 海水又蓝又清。
examples.pinyin: Hǎishuǐ yòu lán yòu qīng.
examples.english: The sea water is blue and clear.

meanings: since (used after a specified time or event)

components.note: 人 (person) — the right-hand part. The left part is a hook-and-dot, from an old tool-like shape. Meaning 'by means of, so as to' is not shown by the parts today.
Memory aid: a person 人 using a tool to get something done — 'by means of' (可以, 所以, 以前). A mnemonic, not proven etymology.
来 (come) — it began as a picture of a wheat plant; the sound was borrowed for "come". 麦 (wheat) still shows it, with a root 夂 added.

example.hanzi: 自从他搬来这里以来,我们成了好朋友。
example.pinyin: Zìcóng tā bān lái zhèlǐ yǐlái, wǒmen chéng le hǎo péngyou.
example.english: Ever since he moved here, we've become good friends.
example.fact: 以来 always looks backward from a past point up to the present, and pairs naturally with 自从 ("ever since") at the front of the clause — it can't be used the way English sometimes stretches "since" toward the future.

examples.hanzi: 毕业以来,我们一直没见过面。
examples.pinyin: Bìyè yǐlái, wǒmen yìzhí méi jiàn guo miàn.
examples.english: We haven't met since graduation.

examples.hanzi: 三个月以来,她每天都坚持跑步。
examples.pinyin: Sān ge yuè yǐlái, tā měi tiān dōu jiānchí pǎobù.
examples.english: For the past three months, she has kept running every day.

components.note: 心 (heart) — a picture of a heart. Written 忄 on the left (快, 怕) and 心 at the bottom (想, 思, 忘); it marks feelings and thoughts.
忄 (heart) — feelings, as in 快 happy, 怕 afraid, 忙 busy.
青 (qīng) is a close sound clue for qíng; the series 清 qīng, 请 qǐng, 晴 qíng, 精 jīng.

example.hanzi: 今天天气很好,我的心情也不错。
example.pinyin: Jīntiān tiānqì hěn hǎo, wǒ de xīnqíng yě búcuò.
example.english: The weather is nice today, and I'm in a good mood too.
example.fact: 心情 names a mood or momentary emotional state, distinct from 性格 ("personality," a lasting trait) — a useful trio to keep straight alongside 感情 ("feelings, an emotional bond between people"), each covering a different slice of "how someone feels."

examples.hanzi: 我今天的心情特别好。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ jīntiān de xīnqíng tèbié hǎo.
examples.english: I'm in an especially good mood today.

examples.hanzi: 你现在有心情看电影吗?
examples.pinyin: Nǐ xiànzài yǒu xīnqíng kàn diànyǐng ma?
examples.english: Are you in the mood to watch a movie now?

components.note: 隹 (zhuī, short-tailed bird) — 难 was first the name of a bird; "hard" is a borrowed use. The 又 here stands in for the traditional left part.
辶 (walk) — movement, as in 这, 近, 送: 过 is to pass or cross.
寸 here replaces 咼 (guō) of the traditional 過, so it is not a sound clue; 咼 survives in 锅 guō and 祸 huò.

example.hanzi: 听到这个坏消息,她很难过。
example.pinyin: Tīngdào zhège huài xiāoxi, tā hěn nánguò.
example.english: Hearing this bad news, she felt very sad.
example.fact: 难过 literally means "hard to get through" (难 "difficult" + 过 "to pass, to cross") — the same logic behind 好过 ("easy to get through, comfortable") — turning a physical image of crossing rough terrain into an emotional description of sadness or hardship.

examples.hanzi: 朋友搬走了,我心里很难过。
examples.pinyin: Péngyou bān zǒu le, wǒ xīnli hěn nánguò.
examples.english: My friend moved away and I feel very sad.

examples.hanzi: 别难过了,明天会更好的。
examples.pinyin: Bié nánguò le, míngtiān huì gèng hǎo de.
examples.english: Don't be sad, tomorrow will be better.

components.note: 土 (earth) — 土 is earth, as in 地, 城; a mold was made of clay, so 型 is a model or type.
刑 (xíng) — same sound — 型 is xíng, like 刑.

example.hanzi: 你是什么血型？
example.pinyin: Nǐ shì shénme xuèxíng?
example.english: What is your blood type?
example.fact: 型 is mainly a suffix: 血型 (blood type), 发型 (hairstyle), 脸型 (face shape), 大型 (large-scale), 型号 (model number). Its original sense was a casting mould.

examples.hanzi: 这个新型手机很受欢迎。
examples.pinyin: Zhège xīnxíng shǒujī hěn shòu huānyíng.
examples.english: This new-model phone is very popular.

examples.hanzi: 这种类型的电影我不爱看。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zhǒng lèixíng de diànyǐng wǒ bú ài kàn.
examples.english: I don't enjoy this type of film.

components.note: 扌 (hand radical, 提手旁) — actions by hand: 打, 拉, 抱; here a hand seizing someone to pass judgment.
卩 (kneeling person) — with 又 hand: sentencing a kneeling prisoner, then answering back: repay, report.

example.hanzi: 我每天早上看报。
example.pinyin: Wǒ měitiān zǎoshang kàn bào.
example.english: I read the newspaper every morning.
example.fact: 报 covers announcing (报告, 报名 to sign up, 报警 to call the police) and a newspaper (看报, 报纸). It also means "to repay": 报答 is to repay a kindness, and 报仇 is to take revenge.

examples.hanzi: 请把这件事报告给经理。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng bǎ zhè jiàn shì bàogào gěi jīnglǐ.
examples.english: Please report this matter to the manager.

examples.hanzi: 我想报名参加汉语班。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng bàomíng cānjiā Hànyǔ bān.
examples.english: I want to sign up for the Chinese class.

components.note: 尸 (roof, body) — 尸 acts as a roof or shelter here, as in 居 and 层; 屋 is a covered place.
至 (arrive) — 至 is where one arrives, so 屋 is a place you get to and stay — a room or house.
子 (child) — a picture of a baby with arms outstretched and legs bundled. As a suffix (孩子, 房子) it is a light noun ending.

example.hanzi: 这个屋子太小了,放不下这张床。
example.pinyin: Zhège wūzi tài xiǎo le, fàng bu xià zhè zhāng chuáng.
example.english: This room is too small to fit this bed.
example.fact: 屋子 and 房间 are near-synonyms for "room," but 屋子 leans more colloquial and spoken while 房间 feels a touch more neutral or formal — a register distinction that rarely survives translation into a single English word "room."

examples.hanzi: 屋子里很暖和。
examples.pinyin: Wūzi lǐ hěn nuǎnhuo.
examples.english: It's warm inside the house.

examples.hanzi: 他在屋子后面种了几棵树。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài wūzi hòumiàn zhòng le jǐ kē shù.
examples.english: He planted a few trees behind the house.

components.note: 刂 (knife) — cutting, as in 到, 分, 别: 制 is cutting to shape, then to make and to control.
辶 (walk, 走之旁) — movement and roads: 过, 进, 送; 造 is to go and make something.
告 (gào) is a loose sound clue (-ao); also in 浩 hào, 靠 kào.

example.hanzi: 这家工厂制造汽车零件。
example.pinyin: Zhè jiā gōngchǎng zhìzào qìchē língjiàn.
example.english: This factory manufactures car parts.
example.fact: 制造 is reserved for tangible, industrial production — cars, machines, weapons — while the near-synonym 制作 covers smaller-scale or artisanal making (a film, a handicraft, a meal); mixing the two is a common slip since English "make" covers both without distinction.

examples.hanzi: 这个工厂每天制造一千台电视机。
examples.pinyin: Zhège gōngchǎng měi tiān zhìzào yì qiān tái diànshìjī.
examples.english: This factory manufactures a thousand TVs every day.

examples.hanzi: 别制造麻烦了,好吗?
examples.pinyin: Bié zhìzào máfan le, hǎo ma?
examples.english: Stop making trouble, okay?

components.note: 玉 (jade) — jade put away safely: 全 first meant flawless, pure, then whole.
阝 (city) — right-side 阝 is 邑 city — 都 is a capital, as in 首都; compare 那, 邮.
者 (zhě) — loose hint — 都 is dū; 者 also sounds out 赌 dǔ and 堵 dǔ, a dū/dǔ series.

example.hanzi: 我说的话他们全都记住了。
example.pinyin: Wǒ shuō de huà tāmen quándōu jìzhù le.
example.english: They remembered everything I said, without exception.
example.fact: 全都 stacks two words that each already mean roughly "all" on their own — 全 ("entire, whole") and 都 ("all, each") — for emphasis; despite the doubling, native speakers don't feel it as redundant the way an English speaker might feel about saying "all entirely."

examples.hanzi: 这些书我全都看过了。
examples.pinyin: Zhèxiē shū wǒ quán dōu kàn guo le.
examples.english: I've read all of these books.

examples.hanzi: 他们全都同意这个办法。
examples.pinyin: Tāmen quán dōu tóngyì zhège bànfǎ.
examples.english: They all agree with this method.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — hand actions, as in 拿, 抱, 把; 打 is to hit.
丁 (dīng) is a loose sound clue for dǎ; 丁 also sounds out 订 dìng, 顶 dǐng and 钉 dīng.
贝 (shell, money) — 贝 is the money radical — 财, 贵, 买, 费; betting stakes money.
者 (zhě) — near hint — 赌 is dǔ; 者 also sounds out 堵 dǔ and 都 dū.

example.hanzi: 我跟你打赌,他一定会来。
example.pinyin: Wǒ gēn nǐ dǎdǔ, tā yídìng huì lái.
example.english: I bet you, he will definitely come.
example.fact: 打 is one of Mandarin's most flexible "light verbs," combining with dozens of otherwise unrelated nouns to form new verbs with little literal connection to "hit" — 打赌 ("to bet"), 打电话 ("to make a phone call"), and 打扫 ("to clean") all lean on the same all-purpose 打.

examples.hanzi: 你敢和我打赌吗?
examples.pinyin: Nǐ gǎn hé wǒ dǎdǔ ma?
examples.english: Do you dare to make a bet with me?

examples.hanzi: 他们打赌谁先到家。
examples.pinyin: Tāmen dǎdǔ shéi xiān dào jiā.
examples.english: They bet on who would get home first.

components.note: 中 (middle) — a line through the middle of a box, a centre mark. 中 gives sound to 钟 zhōng, 种 zhǒng, 忠 zhōng and 衷 zhōng.
门 (gate) — doors and openings, as in 问 ask, 开 open, 关 close.
日 (sun) — a gap in the gate lets daylight through (the traditional 間 had 月 moon): the space between.

example.hanzi: 他坐在我和她中间。
example.pinyin: Tā zuò zài wǒ hé tā zhōngjiān.
example.english: He sits between me and her.
example.fact: 中间 nearly always follows the noun(s) it locates rather than preceding them — 我们中间 ("among us"), 两者中间 ("between the two") — the reverse of English "between us," a pattern shared by most Chinese words of relative position (上面, 下面, 里面).

examples.hanzi: 学校在公园和超市中间。
examples.pinyin: Xuéxiào zài gōngyuán hé chāoshì zhōngjiān.
examples.english: The school is between the park and the supermarket.

examples.hanzi: 我们把桌子放在房间中间吧。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen bǎ zhuōzi fàng zài fángjiān zhōngjiān ba.
examples.english: Let's put the table in the middle of the room.

components.note: 辶 (movement, road) — 辶 marks going and moving, as in 过, 进, 送; 退 is to step back.

example.hanzi: 请往后退一步。
example.pinyin: Qǐng wǎng hòu tuì yí bù.
example.english: Please take one step back.
example.fact: 退 goes beyond retreating to "giving back": 退钱 (refund), 退货 (return goods), 退票 (return a ticket). 退休 means to retire from work, and 后退 means to move backwards.

examples.hanzi: 他退了一步，让我先走。
examples.pinyin: Tā tuìle yí bù, ràng wǒ xiān zǒu.
examples.english: He stepped back to let me go first.

examples.hanzi: 这件衣服太小，我想去退货。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiàn yīfu tài xiǎo, wǒ xiǎng qù tuìhuò.
examples.english: This clothing is too small; I want to return it.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — mouth radical for speaking and sounds, as in 吃, 叫, 吗; 唱 is to sing.
昌 (chāng) — same sound, different tone — 唱 is chàng; 昌 also sounds out 倡 chàng.
欠 (yawn, open mouth) — 欠 shows a person with an open mouth, as in 吹 blow, 欢 joyful; 歌 is the mouth opened in song.
哥 (gē) — same sound — 歌 is gē, just like 哥; 哥 means elder brother.

example.hanzi: 她喜欢在洗澡的时候唱歌。
example.pinyin: Tā xǐhuan zài xǐzǎo de shíhou chànggē.
example.english: She likes to sing while showering.
example.fact: 唱歌 is a verb-object compound that's already grammatically complete on its own — to specify what song, Chinese has to reinsert an object around it (唱一首歌, "sing a song"; 唱这首歌, "sing this song"), since 歌 is already used up inside the fixed verb phrase.

examples.hanzi: 我们一起去唱歌吧!
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen yìqǐ qù chànggē ba!
examples.english: Let's go sing together!

examples.hanzi: 他不太会唱歌,但很喜欢听歌。
examples.pinyin: Tā bú tài huì chànggē, dàn hěn xǐhuan tīng gē.
examples.english: He can't sing very well, but he loves listening to songs.

components.note: 目 (eye) — a cap pulled over the eyes: to cover, to push ahead blindly. Used in 冒险 and 感冒.

example.hanzi: 杯子里冒着热气。
example.pinyin: Bēizi lǐ mào zhe rèqì.
example.english: Steam is rising from the cup.
example.fact: 冒 means to rise or emerge: 冒烟 (give off smoke), 冒汗 (break into a sweat). It also means to brave (冒险, adventure) or to fake (冒牌, counterfeit), and 感冒 is the ordinary word for a cold.

examples.hanzi: 他一说话就冒冷汗。
examples.pinyin: Tā yì shuōhuà jiù mào lěnghàn.
examples.english: He breaks into a cold sweat whenever he speaks.

examples.hanzi: 他冒着雨去上班。
examples.pinyin: Tā màozhe yǔ qù shàngbān.
examples.english: He went to work braving the rain.

components.note: 亻 (person) — person radical — 伦 is about human relations and order, 伦理 ethics.
仑 (lún) — same sound — 仑 also sounds out 轮 lún and 论 lùn.
攵 (tap, strike) — 攵 is a hand holding a stick, in verbs of action, as in 教, 放, 收; 敦 itself mostly appears in 伦敦 London.
享 (xiǎng) — the left part is not a reliable sound clue; 敦 dūn is the clue in 墩 dūn and 蹲 dūn.

example.hanzi: 她去年搬到伦敦工作了。
example.pinyin: Tā qùnián bān dào Lúndūn gōngzuò le.
example.english: She moved to London to work last year.
example.fact: 伦敦 is a straightforward sound-based transliteration of "London," with no attempt at meaningful characters — unlike place names that mix sound and sense, both 伦 and 敦 were chosen purely for how closely they approximate the English syllables.

examples.hanzi: 伦敦的冬天又冷又潮湿。
examples.pinyin: Lúndūn de dōngtiān yòu lěng yòu cháoshī.
examples.english: Winter in London is cold and damp.

examples.hanzi: 我想坐飞机去伦敦旅游。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng zuò fēijī qù Lúndūn lǚyóu.
examples.english: I want to fly to London for a trip.

components.note: 至 (arrive) — oldest form is an arrow landing on a mark: to reach. 至 sounds out 到 dào and 致 zhì, and sits in 室 shì room and 屋 wū.

example.hanzi: 从早上八点至晚上六点营业。
example.pinyin: Cóng zǎoshang bā diǎn zhì wǎnshang liù diǎn yíngyè.
example.english: Open from 8 a.m. to 6 p.m.
example.fact: 至 is the formal counterpart of 到 for "to / until", common on signs and schedules. It also builds 至少 (at least), 至今 (until now), 甚至 (even) and 至于 (as for).

examples.hanzi: 从周一至周五，我都要上班。
examples.pinyin: Cóng zhōuyī zhì zhōuwǔ, wǒ dōu yào shàngbān.
examples.english: I work from Monday through Friday.

examples.hanzi: 这个地方至今还保持着老样子。
examples.pinyin: Zhège dìfang zhìjīn hái bǎochí zhe lǎo yàngzi.
examples.english: This place still keeps its old look to this day.

components.note: 牛 (ox) — cattle and animals, as in 物 thing, 牧 herd, 牺 sacrifice: 特 first meant a bull, then special.
寺 (sì) is only a loose sound clue for tè; 寺 also in 诗 shī and 持 chí.
工 (work) — a carpenter's tool shape: work, craftsman. 工 is a sound series: 红 hóng, 江 jiāng, 功 gōng, 空 kōng.

example.hanzi: 电影里的那个特工成功地完成了任务。
example.pinyin: Diànyǐng lǐ de nàge tègōng chénggōng de wánchéng le rènwu.
example.english: The secret agent in the movie successfully completed the mission.
example.fact: 特工 pairs the "special, set apart" root 特 (also seen in 特殊, elsewhere in this batch) with 工 ("work") — literally "special-duty work[er]" — much as the near-synonym 特务 ("special affairs") compresses to the same core meaning, "secret agent."

examples.hanzi: 他是一名年轻的特工。
examples.pinyin: Tā shì yì míng niánqīng de tègōng.
examples.english: He is a young secret agent.

examples.hanzi: 那个特工一直在暗中保护她。
examples.pinyin: Nà ge tègōng yìzhí zài ànzhōng bǎohù tā.
examples.english: That agent has been protecting her in secret all along.

components.note: 钅 (metal) — 钅 is the simplified 金 (metal), as in 钱, 铁; 镇 first meant to weigh down with metal.
真 (zhēn) — near sound — 镇 is zhèn; 真 also sounds out 慎 shèn and 填 tián.

example.hanzi: 这个小镇很安静。
example.pinyin: Zhège xiǎozhèn hěn ānjìng.
example.english: This little town is very quiet.
example.fact: 镇 began as pressing down with a weight; the "town" meaning came from a garrison holding an area. It is now the administrative level 乡镇, and also forms 镇静 (calm) and 冰镇 (chilled with ice).

examples.hanzi: 这个小镇有一条河。
examples.pinyin: Zhège xiǎozhèn yǒu yì tiáo hé.
examples.english: This small town has a river.

examples.hanzi: 他一直很镇静，没有慌张。
examples.pinyin: Tā yìzhí hěn zhènjìng, méiyǒu huāngzhāng.
examples.english: He stayed calm and did not panic.

components.note: 亻 (person radical, 单人旁) — people and what they do: 你, 他, 位; 停 is a person stopping.
亭 (tíng) sounds exactly like 停; same part in 婷 tíng.
车 (cart) — simplified from 車, a wheeled cart seen from above. As a radical it marks vehicles: 转 turn, 轮 wheel, 较.

example.hanzi: 这里不可以停车。
example.pinyin: Zhèlǐ bù kěyǐ tíngchē.
example.english: You can't park here.
example.fact: 停车 is a fixed verb-object compound (停 "to stop" + 车 "vehicle"), so naming a location often means putting it before the verb rather than tacking it on after, as English does — 在路边停车 ("park by the roadside"), literally "at the roadside, stop-vehicle."

examples.hanzi: 请在门口停车,不要停在路上。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng zài ménkǒu tíngchē, bú yào tíng zài lù shang.
examples.english: Please park at the entrance, not on the road.

examples.hanzi: 你可以在这里停车吗?
examples.pinyin: Nǐ kěyǐ zài zhèlǐ tíngchē ma?
examples.english: Can you park here?

components.note: 将 (jiāng) is the trimmed top part: 奖 jiǎng sounds like 桨 jiǎng and 浆 jiāng.

example.hanzi: 他得了一个大奖。
example.pinyin: Tā dé le yí ge dà jiǎng.
example.english: He won a big prize.
example.fact: 奖 is a prize and also to reward: 奖励 (reward), 奖学金 (scholarship), 中奖 (to win a lottery prize) and 夸奖 (to praise). 诺贝尔奖 is the Nobel Prize.

examples.hanzi: 他在比赛中获得了第一名的奖。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài bǐsài zhōng huòdé le dì-yī míng de jiǎng.
examples.english: He won the first-place prize in the competition.

examples.hanzi: 老师经常夸奖他。
examples.pinyin: Lǎoshī jīngcháng kuājiǎng tā.
examples.english: The teacher often praises him.

components.note: 隹 (short-tailed bird) — bird element as in 难, 谁, 集; in 雇 it is historical, so just treat it as a part.
户 (hù) — sounds out 雇 gù — close (same final, h→g); 户 also sounds out 顾 gù, so 雇 and 顾 sound alike.

example.hanzi: 他们雇了一个司机。
example.pinyin: Tāmen gù le yí ge sījī.
example.english: They hired a driver.
example.fact: 雇 means to hire someone for pay, and 雇主 is the employer. It is used for hiring labour such as drivers, helpers and cleaners; for formal staff appointments Chinese uses 聘 instead.

examples.hanzi: 这家餐厅雇了五个服务员。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā cāntīng gù le wǔ gè fúwùyuán.
examples.english: This restaurant hired five waiters.

examples.hanzi: 我们请了一个雇工帮忙。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen qǐng le yí gè gùgōng bāngmáng.
examples.english: We asked a hired hand to help.

components.note: 戈 (spear) — two hands (廾) holding a spear: guarding against danger — hence warn, abstain, and 戒指 ring, from the old sense of guarding.
扌 (hand radical, 提手旁) — actions by hand: 打, 拉, 抱; 指 is the finger or to point.
旨 (zhǐ) sounds exactly like 指; also in 脂 zhī.

example.hanzi: 他送给她一枚戒指作为生日礼物。
example.pinyin: Tā sòng gěi tā yì méi jièzhi zuòwéi shēngrì lǐwù.
example.english: He gave her a ring as a birthday present.
example.fact: 戒 by itself means "to guard against, to give up (a habit)," as in 戒烟 ("to quit smoking") — only in the compound 戒指 does it take on the narrower sense of a finger ring, which one popular explanation traces to a reminder-band once meant to "guard" the wearer against forgetting a vow or warning.

examples.hanzi: 她手上戴着一枚金色的戒指。
examples.pinyin: Tā shǒu shang dài zhe yì méi jīnsè de jièzhi.
examples.english: She is wearing a gold ring on her hand.

examples.hanzi: 这枚戒指是奶奶留给我的。
examples.pinyin: Zhè méi jièzhi shì nǎinai liú gěi wǒ de.
examples.english: This ring was left to me by my grandma.

components.note: 回 (return) — a swirl or whirlpool drawn as nested squares: it turns around and comes back.
页 (head, page) — in traditional 頭 (豆 + 页): 页 is an old picture of a head, as in 顶, 领, 额. 头 dropped both parts.
大 (big) — the bottom. Memory aid: a big 大 body with two dots ⺀ like eyes above — the head, as in 头发. The dictionary's reading is loose.

example.hanzi: 她听到有人叫她,回头看了一下。
example.pinyin: Tā tīngdào yǒurén jiào tā, huítóu kàn le yíxià.
example.english: She heard someone call her and turned her head to look.
example.fact: Beyond its literal sense of turning one's head, 回头 has drifted into a common colloquial way of saying "later" (回头再说, "let's talk about it later") — the same shift from a physical action to an abstract time reference behind English "in a bit," literally a small piece, meaning "soon."

examples.hanzi: 他一回头,发现后面没有人。
examples.pinyin: Tā yì huítóu, fāxiàn hòumiàn méiyǒu rén.
examples.english: When he turned around, he found no one behind him.

examples.hanzi: 这件事我们回头再说吧。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiàn shì wǒmen huítóu zài shuō ba.
examples.english: Let's talk about this later.

components.note: 冫 (ice, two drops) — marks cold and freezing, as in 冷 cold, 冻 freeze, 凉 cool; 冰 is 冫 plus 水 water: frozen water.

example.hanzi: 请给我一杯冰水。
example.pinyin: Qǐng gěi wǒ yì bēi bīngshuǐ.
example.english: Please give me a glass of iced water.
example.fact: 冰 stands for both ice and iced drinks: 冰咖啡, 冰淇淋 (ice cream). Many Chinese people prefer hot or warm drinks, so asking for 冰水 can feel unusual. 冰箱 is the refrigerator and 冰山 an iceberg.

examples.hanzi: 夏天我喜欢喝冰咖啡。
examples.pinyin: Xiàtiān wǒ xǐhuan hē bīng kāfēi.
examples.english: In summer I like to drink iced coffee.

examples.hanzi: 河面结了冰。
examples.pinyin: Hémiàn jié le bīng.
examples.english: The river surface has frozen over.

components.note: 礻 (altar, spirit — form of 示) — rites and prayer: 神, 礼, 福, 祈; 祝 is to wish.
兄 (older brother) — an opened mouth before the altar: the one who speaks the prayer or blessing.
贝 (shell, money) — 贝 is the money/gift radical — congratulating often meant sending a gift; compare 财, 买.
加 (jiā) — 加 means add and was the sound clue; today the sound has drifted (贺 is hè).

example.hanzi: 我要祝贺你顺利通过考试。
example.pinyin: Wǒ yào zhùhè nǐ shùnlì tōngguò kǎoshì.
example.english: I want to congratulate you on passing the exam successfully.
example.fact: 贺 alone traces back to adding (加) something valuable (贝, "money, shell currency") onto someone's good fortune — a literal gift piled onto their luck — which is why 祝贺 pairs naturally with an occasion worth celebrating (毕业, 生日, 结婚) rather than casual good news.

examples.hanzi: 祝贺你找到了新工作!
examples.pinyin: Zhùhè nǐ zhǎodào le xīn gōngzuò!
examples.english: Congratulations on finding a new job!

examples.hanzi: 大家都来祝贺他们结婚。
examples.pinyin: Dàjiā dōu lái zhùhè tāmen jiéhūn.
examples.english: Everyone came to congratulate them on their wedding.

components.note: 氵 (water, 三点水) — marks water and liquids, as in 海 sea, 汤 soup; a hole as eroded by flowing water.
同 (tóng) — sound hint is loose (dòng vs tóng); 同 also sounds out 铜 tóng and 筒 tǒng.

example.hanzi: 墙上有一个洞。
example.pinyin: Qiáng shang yǒu yí ge dòng.
example.english: There is a hole in the wall.
example.fact: 洞 is also the radio and military spoken form of the digit 0, when numbers must not be confused: 洞 (0), 幺 (1), 拐 (7). It forms 山洞 (cave), 洞穴 (cavern) and 黑洞 (black hole).

examples.hanzi: 这个洞太小了，我进不去。
examples.pinyin: Zhège dòng tài xiǎo le, wǒ jìn bu qù.
examples.english: This hole is too small for me to get in.

examples.hanzi: 山里有一个很深的山洞。
examples.pinyin: Shān lǐ yǒu yí gè hěn shēn de shāndòng.
examples.english: There is a very deep cave in the mountains.

components.note: 木 (tree) — wood, as in 桌, 树, 板: 案 is a wooden table.
安 (ān) is a close sound clue for àn; also in 按 àn.
亻 (person radical, 单人旁) — people and what they do: 你, 他, 位.
牛 (ox) — in the traditional reading, a person 亻 dividing up an ox: one piece, hence 件 as a measure word for items.

example.hanzi: 警察正在调查这起案件。
example.pinyin: Jǐngchá zhèngzài diàochá zhè qǐ ànjiàn.
example.english: The police are investigating this case.
example.fact: 案件 is reserved for a legal or criminal matter under investigation — a police case, a court case — and would sound strange applied to an everyday "case" as in "in that case," which Chinese instead expresses with an entirely different word, 情况 or 如果.

examples.hanzi: 这起案件已经有了新进展。
examples.pinyin: Zhè qǐ ànjiàn yǐjīng yǒu le xīn jìnzhǎn.
examples.english: This case has already made new progress.

examples.hanzi: 法官今天要审理一件重要的案件。
examples.pinyin: Fǎguān jīntiān yào shěnlǐ yí jiàn zhòngyào de ànjiàn.
examples.english: The judge will hear an important case today.

components.note: 木 (wood, tree) — 条 was a long slender twig, so branch, strip, and then the measure word for long things; 木 as in 树, 板.
亻 (person radical, 单人旁) — people and what they do: 你, 他, 位.
牛 (ox) — in the traditional reading, a person 亻 dividing up an ox: one piece, hence 件 as a measure word for items.

example.hanzi: 他答应了,但提出了一个条件。
example.pinyin: Tā dāying le, dàn tíchū le yí gè tiáojiàn.
example.english: He agreed, but put forward one condition.
example.fact: 条件 shares its second character 件 with 案件 (also in this batch) — 件 works as a measure word for discrete items and matters, so both words literally count off individual, itemized "pieces" of something, whether legal cases or the separate stipulations of an agreement.

examples.hanzi: 只要条件允许,我就去旅行。
examples.pinyin: Zhǐyào tiáojiàn yǔnxǔ, wǒ jiù qù lǚxíng.
examples.english: As long as conditions allow, I'll go travel.

examples.hanzi: 这家公司给员工的条件很好。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā gōngsī gěi yuángōng de tiáojiàn hěn hǎo.
examples.english: This company offers its employees very good terms.

components.note: 亻 (person) — people, as in 你, 他, 做: 作 is something a person does or makes.
乍 (zuò) gives the exact sound; 乍 also in 昨 zuó, 炸 zhà and 怎 zěn.
口 (mouth) — three mouths: many goods and people speaking; hence products, quality, and to taste. Also in 品尝 and 作品.

example.hanzi: 这是她最有名的一部作品。
example.pinyin: Zhè shì tā zuì yǒumíng de yí bù zuòpǐn.
example.english: This is her most famous work.
example.fact: 品, tripling the mouth radical 口, originally suggested many people tasting, judging, or ranking something — 作品 ("a work that's been made") keeps a faint trace of that sense, a finished piece put up for others to judge and appraise.

examples.hanzi: 这部作品花了她三年时间。
examples.pinyin: Zhè bù zuòpǐn huā le tā sān nián shíjiān.
examples.english: This work took her three years.

examples.hanzi: 我很喜欢这位作家的作品。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ hěn xǐhuan zhè wèi zuòjiā de zuòpǐn.
examples.english: I really like this writer's works.

components.note: 艹 (grass) — on top, but in 若 it is most likely a worn-down picture of hair, not plants; oracle forms show a person smoothing hair, meaning 'to yield'.
右 (right hand) — below. 若 is the sound part of 诺 nuò promise and 惹 rě, loosely; used for 'if' (若是), 'like' (若无其事).

example.hanzi: 若有问题，请告诉我。
example.pinyin: Ruò yǒu wèntí, qǐng gàosu wǒ.
example.english: If you have any problem, please tell me.
example.fact: 若 is the written-style "if", more formal than 如果; you will see it on notices and in literature. It also appears in 若干 (several), 若无其事 (as if nothing had happened) and 假若 (supposing).

examples.hanzi: 若你有时间，请来看我。
examples.pinyin: Ruò nǐ yǒu shíjiān, qǐng lái kàn wǒ.
examples.english: If you have time, please come see me.

examples.hanzi: 他若不来，我们就先走。
examples.pinyin: Tā ruò bù lái, wǒmen jiù xiān zǒu.
examples.english: If he doesn't come, we'll leave first.

components.note: 手 (hand) — a picture of a hand with fingers spread. As a left-hand radical it becomes 扌 in 打 hit, 拿 take, 推 push.
田 (field) — farmland, the village's fields.
土 (earth) — land; field + earth gives "village" and then the unit of distance. 里 is the sound part of 理 lǐ.

example.hanzi: 他手里拿着一本书。
example.pinyin: Tā shǒulǐ ná zhe yì běn shū.
example.english: He's holding a book in his hand.
example.fact: 手里 extends beyond the literal hand to mean "in someone's control or possession" — 钱在他手里 ("the money is in his hands," i.e. under his control) — the same metaphor English uses when it says a decision is "in someone's hands."

examples.hanzi: 他手里还有一点儿钱。
examples.pinyin: Tā shǒu lǐ hái yǒu yìdiǎnr qián.
examples.english: He still has a little money on hand.

examples.hanzi: 这件事现在在老板手里。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiàn shì xiànzài zài lǎobǎn shǒu lǐ.
examples.english: This matter is now in the boss's hands.

components.note: 友 (friend) replaces the heart-and-foot lower part of the traditional 愛, which had 心 (heart); so 爱 lost its heart in simplification.
上 (above) — a mark above a line, the mirror of 下 below.

example.hanzi: 他们在大学的时候爱上了对方。
example.pinyin: Tāmen zài dàxué de shíhou àishàng le duìfāng.
example.english: They fell in love with each other in university.
example.fact: 上 tacked onto a verb often marks the moment an action successfully "sticks" or takes hold — 爱上 ("fall in love with"), 看上 ("take a liking to"), 迷上 ("become obsessed with") — a small but very productive verb-complement pattern worth learning as a set.

examples.hanzi: 她很快就爱上了这座小城。
examples.pinyin: Tā hěn kuài jiù àishàng le zhè zuò xiǎochéng.
examples.english: She soon fell in love with this little town.

examples.hanzi: 我爱上了跑步,每天都不想停。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ àishàng le pǎobù, měi tiān dōu bù xiǎng tíng.
examples.english: I've fallen in love with running and don't want to stop each day.

components.note: 刂 (knife) — cutting and sharp edges: 利 sharp, 刻 carve, 别 divide; 则 meant rules engraved to last. 贝 here is simplified from old 鼎.

example.hanzi: 他喜欢甜的，我则喜欢咸的。
example.pinyin: Tā xǐhuan tián de, wǒ zé xǐhuan xián de.
example.english: He likes sweet, whereas I like salty.
example.fact: As a conjunction 则 contrasts or follows on: "whereas", "then". As a noun it is a rule: 规则, 原则, and 否则 means "otherwise". It is also a measure word for items of news or short texts: 一则新闻.

examples.hanzi: 这是我们的规则，大家要遵守。
examples.pinyin: Zhè shì wǒmen de guīzé, dàjiā yào zūnshǒu.
examples.english: These are our rules, and everyone must follow them.

examples.hanzi: 他喜欢踢球，我则爱看书。
examples.pinyin: Tā xǐhuan tīqiú, wǒ zé ài kàn shū.
examples.english: He likes playing ball, while I prefer reading.

components.note: 木 (wood) — wooden things: 桌, 板, 架; 档 is a wooden shelf for files.
当 (dāng) is a near sound match for dàng; also in 挡 dǎng.
木 (tree) — wood, as in 桌, 树, 板: 案 is a wooden table.
安 (ān) is a close sound clue for àn; also in 按 àn.

example.hanzi: 这些档案都保存在地下室里。
example.pinyin: Zhèxiē dàng'àn dōu bǎocún zài dìxiàshì lǐ.
example.english: These files are all kept in the basement.
example.fact: 档案 shares its second character 案 with 案件 (also in this batch) — both trace back to 案's original sense of a wooden table or desk, the surface where documents were once laid out, filed, and reviewed.

examples.hanzi: 请把这份档案交给经理。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng bǎ zhè fèn dàng'àn jiāo gěi jīnglǐ.
examples.english: Please hand this file to the manager.

examples.hanzi: 我在电脑里建了一个新档案。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ zài diànnǎo lǐ jiàn le yí ge xīn dàng'àn.
examples.english: I created a new file on my computer.

components.note: 千 (thousand) — 千 is a number built on the old form of 人 with an extra stroke; its sound is also in 迁 qiān.
萬 (traditional ten thousand) — 万 is the simplified form of 萬, which pictured a scorpion borrowed for the number 10,000; 万 also sounds out 迈 mài.

example.hanzi: 你千万不要告诉他这个秘密。
example.pinyin: Nǐ qiānwàn bú yào gàosu tā zhège mìmì.
example.english: Whatever you do, don't tell him this secret.
example.fact: Beyond its literal sense "ten million," 千万 has a second, seemingly unrelated use as an emphatic adverb meaning "whatever you do" — almost always paired with a negative command (千万不要..., "whatever you do, don't...") to add urgency to a warning.

examples.hanzi: 这件事千万不能忘记。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiàn shì qiānwàn bù néng wàngjì.
examples.english: You must not forget this under any circumstances.

examples.hanzi: 千万别在路上玩手机!
examples.pinyin: Qiānwàn bié zài lù shang wán shǒujī!
examples.english: Whatever you do, don't play with your phone on the road!

components.note: 土 (earth) — the top part, the ground family as in 地, 场, 块. Memory aid: leave the ground 土 and go off on your own 厶 path.
厶 (private, small loop) — the bottom part. Old forms show a person leaving a place, so the 土 story is only a mnemonic.
世 (generation) — from 卅 (thirty): about thirty years is one generation, so an age or the world.

example.hanzi: 他的祖父去年去世了。
example.pinyin: Tā de zǔfù qùnián qùshì le.
example.english: His grandfather passed away last year.
example.fact: 去世 is a polite, formal euphemism for dying — literally "to leave the world" — sitting alongside other registers for death in Chinese, from the blunt 死 to the more elevated 逝世 reserved for public figures, each carrying a different degree of formality and respect.

examples.hanzi: 他的爷爷去世以后,奶奶一个人住。
examples.pinyin: Tā de yéye qùshì yǐhòu, nǎinai yí ge rén zhù.
examples.english: After his grandfather passed away, grandma lived alone.

examples.hanzi: 听说那位老教授昨天去世了。
examples.pinyin: Tīngshuō nà wèi lǎo jiàoshòu zuótiān qùshì le.
examples.english: I heard that old professor passed away yesterday.
